question: Why do mixtures of water and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium iodide with water content below and above 50 mol percent exhibit distinct trends in density and melting point?
answer: Mixtures of water and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium iodide with water content below and above 50 mol percent exhibit distinct trends in density and melting point due to differences in molecular ordering. At low water concentrations, water molecules integrate into the ordered cation-anion structure of the ionic liquid, maintaining density and increasing melting point slightly. Above 50 mol percent water, this molecular ordering breaks down, leading to a dramatic drop in density and a rapid increase in melting point, as the mixture transitions to a state resembling water with regions of ionic liquid dissolved within.
